states.label: Invites table
states.title: Store invites
states.problem: Nothing records who was invited to a team.
states.approach: Add an invites table with a token and an expiry date.
states.outcome: An invites table with a token, the team and an expiry date.

states.label: Migration rolls back
states.title: Undo the table cleanly
states.problem: A migration that only goes forward is hard to undo in production.
states.approach: Write the down migration and run both ways.
states.outcome: The migration runs forward and back on a copy of the database.

states.label: Send an invite
states.title: Invite someone by email
states.problem: Only an admin can add people today, by hand.
states.approach: Add an endpoint that stores the invite and sends the email.
states.outcome: POST /teams/:id/invites stores the invite and sends the email.

states.label: Accept an invite
states.title: Join from the link
states.problem: The link in the email has to add the person to the team.
states.approach: Check the token, then add the member.
states.outcome: The link checks the token, adds the member, and answers 410 once it has expired.

states.label: Expire old invites
states.title: Old links stop working
states.problem: An invite link should not work forever.
states.approach: A nightly job expires invites older than 7 days.

states.label: Limit sends
states.title: No invite floods
states.problem: One account could send thousands of emails.
states.approach: Allow 50 invites a day per team.

states.label: Invite form
states.title: Invite from the team page
states.problem: There is nowhere to type an email.
states.approach: A form on the team page, with errors inline.

states.label: Pending invites
states.title: See who has not joined
states.problem: Admins cannot tell who still has to accept.
states.approach: List pending invites with resend and cancel.

states.label: Invite email
states.title: A clear email
states.problem: The invite has to say who sent it and to which team.
states.approach: A short email with one button.

states.label: End-to-end
states.title: The whole path works
states.problem: Each part passes alone, but nothing tests the path from email to team.
states.approach: A browser test that invites, accepts and checks the team.

states.label: Behind a flag
states.title: Turn it on slowly
states.problem: A problem should not reach every team at once.
states.approach: Ship it behind a flag, off by default.

states.label: Document invites
states.title: Explain invites
states.problem: Admins need to know the limits and the expiry.
states.approach: Add a page to the admin guide.

active.label: Expire old invites
active.title: Old links stop working
active.problem: An invite link should not work forever.
active.approach: A nightly job expires invites older than 7 days.

instructions.name: depth-before-size
instructions.title: Deeper, not bigger
instructions.text: Before you write the plan, answer in a few lines: what would an expert in this field do here that the brief doesn't ask for; what is the rawest material to start from (the real failing output, the files, the logs) instead of a summary; which methods and tools would they use; and what, other than you or the user, shows the result is right (name the artifact). Put the answers at the top of the plan as choices the user can take or leave.

instructions.name: fast-checks
instructions.title: Fastest check that proves it
instructions.text: Give this state the fastest check that proves its work: one test file, a type check or a build. Leave whole suites for the final checks.

instructions.name: failure-list
instructions.title: Failure list first
instructions.text: Before writing logic, write down how it can fail and test each item, with the tests written before the code. Tests written after the code to raise coverage end up restating it.

instructions.name: fails-first
instructions.title: Check fails before the work
instructions.text: Sentinel runs the state's check once before any edit. If it already passes, Claude is told the check proves nothing yet and tightens it.

instructions.name: break-it-once
instructions.title: A test must be able to fail
instructions.text: Break the code each new test targets once and watch the test fail, then put the code back. Report any test you couldn't make fail.

instructions.name: fails-without-change
instructions.title: Check fails without the change
instructions.text: Before a state closes, Sentinel reruns its check in a scratch copy that has the state's test changes but not its code changes. If the check still passes there, the advance is refused until the check is tightened or Claude records why with decide. If it fails, Sentinel runs it once more with the code changes in, to tell a real failure from a copy that can't run the check.

instructions.name: prove-end-to-end
instructions.title: Prove it end to end
instructions.text: A feature that crosses parts ends with an end-to-end run that leaves an artifact anyone can rerun and a script can check: the command and its saved output, a rendered image, a log.

instructions.name: measure-before-delete
instructions.title: Delete tests only after measuring
instructions.needs: A mutation-testing tool, such as Stryker or go-mutesting.
instructions.text: Delete a test only after a mutation run shows it catches nothing the others don't. Never by reading alone.

instructions.name: sources-first
instructions.title: Plan from the raw sources
instructions.text: Plan from the raw sources (the TRD, the design frames, the sprint sheet), not summaries of them. Where they disagree, the TRD decides behaviour and data, the design decides screens, and the sprint sheet decides scope and order. List each conflict at the top of the plan, and ask before departing from the TRD on anything structural.

instructions.text: Before you write the plan, answer in a few lines: what would an expert in this field do here that the brief doesn't ask for; what is the rawest material to start from (the real failing output, the files, the logs) instead of a summary; which methods and tools would they use; and what, other than you or the user, shows the result is right (name the artifact). Put the answers at the top of the plan as choices the user can take or leave.

instructions.name: fast-checks
instructions.title: Fastest check that proves it
instructions.text: Give this state the fastest check that proves its work: one test file, a type check or a build. Leave whole suites for the final checks.

instructions.name: failure-list
instructions.title: Failure list first
instructions.text: Before writing logic, write down how it can fail and test each item, with the tests written before the code. Tests written after the code to raise coverage end up restating it.

instructions.name: fails-first
instructions.title: Check fails before the work
instructions.text: Sentinel runs the state's check once before any edit. If it already passes, Claude is told the check proves nothing yet and tightens it.

instructions.name: break-it-once
instructions.title: A test must be able to fail
instructions.text: Break the code each new test targets once and watch the test fail, then put the code back. Report any test you couldn't make fail.

instructions.name: fails-without-change
instructions.title: Check fails without the change
instructions.text: Before a state closes, Sentinel reruns its check in a scratch copy that has the state's test changes but not its code changes. If the check still passes there, the advance is refused until the check is tightened or Claude records why with decide. If it fails, Sentinel runs it once more with the code changes in, to tell a real failure from a copy that can't run the check.

instructions.name: prove-end-to-end
instructions.title: Prove it end to end
instructions.text: A feature that crosses parts ends with an end-to-end run that leaves an artifact anyone can rerun and a script can check: the command and its saved output, a rendered image, a log.

instructions.name: measure-before-delete
instructions.title: Delete tests only after measuring
instructions.needs: A mutation-testing tool, such as Stryker or go-mutesting.
instructions.text: Delete a test only after a mutation run shows it catches nothing the others don't. Never by reading alone.

instructions.name: sources-first
instructions.title: Plan from the raw sources
instructions.text: Plan from the raw sources (the TRD, the design frames, the sprint sheet), not summaries of them. Where they disagree, the TRD decides behaviour and data, the design decides screens, and the sprint sheet decides scope and order. List each conflict at the top of the plan, and ask before departing from the TRD on anything structural.

states.title: Fix the accepted findings

states.label: Invites table
states.title: Store invites
states.problem: Nothing records who was invited to a team.
states.approach: Add an invites table with a token and an expiry date.
states.outcome: An invites table with a token, the team and an expiry date.

states.label: Migration rolls back
states.title: Undo the table cleanly
states.problem: A migration that only goes forward is hard to undo in production.
states.approach: Write the down migration and run both ways.
states.outcome: The migration runs forward and back on a copy of the database.

states.label: Send an invite
states.title: Invite someone by email
states.problem: Only an admin can add people today, by hand.
states.approach: Add an endpoint that stores the invite and sends the email.
states.outcome: POST /teams/:id/invites stores the invite and sends the email.

states.label: Accept an invite
states.title: Join from the link
states.problem: The link in the email has to add the person to the team.
states.approach: Check the token, then add the member.
states.outcome: The link checks the token, adds the member, and answers 410 once it has expired.

states.label: Expire old invites
states.title: Old links stop working
states.problem: An invite link should not work forever.
states.approach: A nightly job expires invites older than 7 days.
states.outcome: A nightly job expires invites after 7 days.

states.label: Limit sends
states.title: No invite floods
states.problem: One account could send thousands of emails.
states.approach: Allow 50 invites a day per team.
states.outcome: Each team can send 50 invites a day; the 51st gets a 429.

states.label: Invite form
states.title: Invite from the team page
states.problem: There is nowhere to type an email.
states.approach: A form on the team page, with errors inline.

states.label: Pending invites
states.title: See who has not joined
states.problem: Admins cannot tell who still has to accept.
states.approach: List pending invites with resend and cancel.

states.label: Invite email
states.title: A clear email
states.problem: The invite has to say who sent it and to which team.
states.approach: A short email with one button.

states.label: End-to-end
states.title: The whole path works
states.problem: Each part passes alone, but nothing tests the path from email to team.
states.approach: A browser test that invites, accepts and checks the team.

states.label: Behind a flag
states.title: Turn it on slowly
states.problem: A problem should not reach every team at once.
states.approach: Ship it behind a flag, off by default.

states.label: Document invites
states.title: Explain invites
states.problem: Admins need to know the limits and the expiry.
states.approach: Add a page to the admin guide.

active.label: Invite form
active.title: Invite from the team page
active.problem: There is nowhere to type an email.
active.approach: A form on the team page, with errors inline.

audit.text: Expired link → Answer 410 with a way to ask for a new invite (A plain error leaves the person stuck.)
accept: +src/api/teams/members.ts (Accepting an invite adds the member to the team.)

log.text: Decided · Expired link → Answer 410 with a way to ask for a new invite (A plain error leaves the person stuck.)
